original_value: Coverage maintenance is a bottleneck restricting the development of underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs). Since the energy of the nodes is limited, the coverage of UASNs may gradually decrease as the network operates. Thus, energy-saving coverage control is crucial for UASNs. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a coverage-control strategy (referred to as ESACC) that establishes a sleep–wake scheduling mechanism based on the redundancy of deployment nodes. The strategy has two main parts: (1) Node sleep scheduling based on a memetic algorithm. To ensure network monitoring performance, only some nodes are scheduled to work, with redundant nodes in a low-power hibernation state, reducing energy consumption and prolonging the network lifetime. The goal of node scheduling is to find a minimum set of nodes that can cover the monitoring area, and a memetic algorithm can solve this problem. (2) Wake-up scheme. During network operation, sleeping nodes are woken to cover the dead nodes and maintain high coverage. This scheme not only reduces the network energy consumption but takes into account the monitoring coverage of the network. The experimental data show that ESACC performs better than current algorithms, and can improve the network life cycle while ensuring high coverage.

result.paraphrase: Coverage maintenance is a major bottleneck in the development of underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs). Because node energy is limited, UASN coverage can gradually decline as the network runs. Therefore, energy-efficient coverage control is essential for UASNs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a coverage-control strategy called ESACC, which builds a sleep–wake scheduling mechanism based on deployment-node redundancy. The strategy consists of two main components: (1) node sleep scheduling using a memetic algorithm. To preserve monitoring performance, only part of the nodes are assigned to operate, while redundant nodes remain in low-power hibernation, lowering energy use and extending network lifetime. The scheduling objective is to identify the minimum set of nodes that can cover the monitored area, a problem that can be solved by a memetic algorithm. (2) A wake-up scheme. During operation, sleeping nodes are activated to cover failed nodes and keep coverage high. This approach not only reduces network energy consumption but also maintains monitoring coverage. Experimental results indicate that ESACC outperforms existing algorithms and can prolong the network lifecycle while ensuring high coverage.
